conventions.envelopes: normalised = raw envelope / session-1 maximum of the channel; raw = un-normalised envelope (mV), decimated to 100 Hz
conventions.target: torque - passive(angle), float32 as the network sees it
conventions.time: t = 1.001 + 0.01 k s since the start of that trial's recording; k = 100 Hz sample after the 1 s trim
conventions.trial_index: df.attrs['trial_index'] = 0-based position in the .flb file (original logs print index+1)

example_window.note: window ends 0.15 s after the start of the third push; same rule as x05

y02.max_definition: validation part = the 1 kHz sample lies where a validation window can see it: 100 Hz sample >= 7131 and <= 8908 ('val_only'; the target-time rule) ; 'touches_validation_windows' also counts 100 Hz samples 7112..7130, which belong to the last fit windows and the first validation windows. Trimmed first second = raw sample < 1000.
y02.n_dropped_window_per_s1_trial_note: int(8891*0.8)=7112 and int(8891*0.2)=1778 leave 1 window (the last of the trial) unused: _temporal_split discards the remainder
y02.normalised_peaks_note: The scale uses the 1 kHz envelope maximum; after the x10 decimation the 100 Hz peak can fall a hair below 1.0. s1_fit_part is what the network sees in the fit windows only.
y02.passive_tables_note: IES has no passive trials: empty tables, nothing is subtracted. YES: typed-in worksheet values (config.PASSIVE_TORQUE_OVERRIDES). Others: auto-detected from the passive holds. Straight lines between the points; outside the measured range the end segments are extended linearly (dataset_builder._extrapolate).

pushes.method: runs where the target < midpoint of its 5th-95th percentile for >= 0.5 s (same rule as x01)

y02.seed_note: no training here; seed0.npz is used only to check the session-2 targets
